resources.string: Without it the game cannot be read and the mods folder cannot be created.
Install the game from Play Store. The patcher works with the copy already on this device and downloads nothing.
%d%% · you can leave the app, it keeps going
The original has to be removed first: the rebuilt one carries a different signature. Worlds and settings stay where they are.
Remove the original first, otherwise the installer reports a damaged package.
The game needs file access too
It asks for it on its own only much later. Granting it now means mods are picked up from the first launch.
Native mods are .so files, script mods are .js, packaged ones are .nrzmod. The loader picks them up when the game starts.
Nothing here yet. Open a .nrzmod file, or drop a mod in and restart the game.
It appears after the modded game runs for the first time: %s
A mod with this name is already installed and will be replaced.
Installed. Restart the game to pick it up.
Windows on top of the game
Mods can draw their own panels over the game — a coordinate readout, a control panel. Android asks for this one separately.
The game was built by an older loader
Inside the game sits loader %1$s, the launcher now carries %2$s. Build the modded version again to bring it up.
Checks whether the game kept the names of its own classes. That answers whether mods can reach the gameplay code at all. Nothing is sent anywhere.
Reading the game library, a minute or so…
A copy of the loader sits next to the mods, and the game prefers it. Updating the launcher is enough — just restart the game. Rebuilding is only needed when the package itself changes.
Is the probe going to work
The loader counts calls to every method of this class and writes reports/slots.txt. LocalPlayer is you — it always exists.
